newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia creditors to meet, no new offer - Kia.
newsitem.headline: Kia creditors to meet, no new offer - Kia.

text.p: Creditors of South Korea's troubled Kia Group were set to meet on Monday afternoon in another attempt to sort out a bail-out plan, but company officials said Kia had nothing new to offer.
"There's been no new development so far in our stance," Kia spokesman Jeun Sang-jin said by telephone. "I don't know whether a separate announcement will be made before the meeting."
The group's creditor banks, which put Kia under protection on July 15, have twice failed to agree on a bail-out programme. They were to meet again at 3.00 p.m. (0600 GMT) on Monday.
Kia, the nation's eighth-largest conglomerate, has some 9.54 trillion won of debts mainly due to slumping domestic sales by its two automaking units -- Kia Motors Corp and Asia Motors Corp.
The group has refused key demands by creditor banks that the group's top executives unconditionally resign and that Asia Motors be sold off to a third party.
Instead, the group has maintained Asia Motors would be absorbed by Kia Motors to serve as assembly plants after selling off assets not directly related to its manufacturing activities.
